title: Historical Ingest Accelerator — semantic dedupe, cost-aware chunking, and partial-apply
creator: Anita Kapoor
description:
Problem: Running full historical reingests for console usage telemetry is expensive, brittle, and slow for large tenants. Current replay tools either reapply everything (high cost) or rely on coarse windowing that causes duplicate or missing derived records. Goal: build an "accelerator" service and CLI that reduces cost and operator toil for tenant-scoped historical ingests by combining semantic deduplication, cost-aware chunking, and safe partial-apply semantics.

Scope and success criteria:
- A reusable service (ingest-accelerator) that orchestrates redo jobs against the analytics pipeline with: tenant-aware chunking, semantic dedupe, resume tokens, idempotent partial apply, and cost/latency telemetry.
- Reduce tokenized compute cost for large backfills by >=40% for typical workloads while keeping derived results bit-for-bit equivalent for high-accuracy workloads and providing an "eventual-correctness" mode for lower-cost runs.
- Provide tools for canarying, dry-run previews, and automated safety checks (schema drift, late-arrival bounds).

Design highlights:
- Chunker: splits a tenant's history into adaptive time+activity chunks using heuristics (burst density, actor cardinality). Chunk sizes expose a cost-estimate and expected runtime per chunk.
- Semantic dedupe layer: builds a fingerprint of events using key fields and a lightweight content hash; supports configurable thresholds for similarity to collapse near-duplicates (useful for noisy telemetry).
- Partial-apply orchestrator: supports applying only changed partitions to downstream materializations (metrics/rollups), with checkpointed resume tokens and idempotent commit markers to avoid double-apply.
- Modes: "Exact" (bit-for-bit where determinism needed), "Heuristic" (semantic dedupe + partial-apply), and "Sampled" (cost-priority sampling for exploratory backfills).
- Safety: mandatory dry-run verification for >10M events, automatic snapshot of downstream state before high-risk runs, and automatic revert/compaction strategy documented and tested.

Interfaces & integrations:
- CLI: redwood-ingest-accelerator run --tenant T --from DATE --to DATE --mode heuristic --chunk-size auto --dry-run
- Orchestration: runs as a Kubernetes Job per chunk with a coordinator service that persists checkpoint state to the reingest-store (Cosmos-style vault).
- Observability: per-chunk metrics (events, estimated cost, duration), artifacts in the Console (backfill-job page), and audit logs for PB/Private customers.

Trade-offs considered:
- Stronger dedupe reduces cost but risks losing subtle event ordering assumptions. We mitigate via conservative defaults and opt-in heuristics per tenant.
- Partial-apply requires downstream materializations to support incremental patching; we add a compatibility shim for older pipelines at higher cost.
- Complexity vs operator UX: initial MVP focuses on clear safe defaults and a concise CLI; advanced knobs hidden under an "expert" flag.

2026-02-22 — Implemented checkpoint schema v1 and resume token format. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-accelerator/pull/127
